rationale: Applied P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT (bound jobs with a custom timeout). The workflow currently relies on GitHub's default 360-minute job timeout with no explicit per-job bound. The repository CI history shows successful runs completing within minutes, and the pattern's preconditions (representative successful-duration history exists) are met. Adding timeout-minutes: 30 to each job bounds runaway consumption while preserving all build and test coverage, with ample operational headroom over observed durations. This is a minimal, non-behavior-changing change that adds no new network access, secrets, or privileged actions. The experiment evidence (batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508) measured a custom timeout reducing elapsed time with all runs still succeeding, and the pattern reports estimated vm-time reductions for both free and paid runners.
